hints: Separate as (sin4y/sin2y) dy = x sin3x dx.
Use sin4y=2sin2y cos2y so the left integral becomes sin2y.
Integrate x sin3x by parts, taking u=x and dv=sin3x dx, and keep both resulting terms.
Apply y=π/12 when x=π/2 using exact trigonometric values to determine the constant, then state the relation.
walkthrough:
Simplify the left-hand side using the double-angle formula $\sin(4y) = 2\sin(2y)\cos(2y)$:
$$\dfrac{2\sin(2y)\cos(2y)}{\sin(2y)}\,\mathrm{d}y = 2\cos(2y)\,\mathrm{d}y$$
$$\int 2\cos(2y)\,\mathrm{d}y = \sin(2y)$$

Integrate the right-hand side $\int x\sin(3x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ using integration by parts:
$$u = x \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = \sin(3x) \implies v = -\dfrac{1}{3}\cos(3x)$$
$$\int x\sin(3x)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{3}x\cos(3x) - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\cos(3x)\right)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{3}x\cos(3x) + \dfrac{1}{9}\sin(3x)$$

Equate the antiderivatives and add the constant of integration $C$:
$$\sin(2y) = -\dfrac{1}{3}x\cos(3x) + \dfrac{1}{9}\sin(3x) + C$$

Determine $C$ using the initial condition $y = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$ when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$\text{Left side: } \sin\left(2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{12}\right) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Right side: } -\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{9}\sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) + C$$
$$\text{Since } \cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = 0 \text{ and } \sin\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right) = -1:$$
$$\dfrac{1}{2} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{9}(-1) + C \implies \dfrac{1}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{9} + C$$
$$C = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{9} = \dfrac{9 + 2}{18} = \dfrac{11}{18}$$

hints: Set x=0 in the relation from part (a) to obtain an equation for sin2y.
Transform 0<y<π/2 into 0<2y<π, so the sine equation has two possible angles.
Find both radian solutions, divide by 2, and give non-exact answers to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Substitute $x = 0$ into the relation from part (a):
$$\sin(2y) = -\dfrac{1}{3}(0)\cos(0) + \dfrac{1}{9}\sin(0) + \dfrac{11}{18} = \dfrac{11}{18} \approx 0.611111$$

Determine the domain for the angle $2y$ given $0 < y < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$0 < 2y < \pi$$

Find the first solution in radians:
$$2y_1 = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{11}{18}\right) \approx 0.657984 \implies y_1 = \dfrac{0.657984}{2} \approx 0.32899 \approx 0.329$$

Find the second solution in the interval $(0, \pi)$:
$$2y_2 = \pi - 0.657984 \approx 3.141593 - 0.657984 = 2.483609 \implies y_2 = \dfrac{2.483609}{2} \approx 1.24180 \approx 1.24$$

State the values of $y$ correct to 3 significant figures:
$$y = 0.329, \quad 1.24$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Solves $\sin2y=\frac{11}{18}$ to derive one solution, e.g. $0.329$; Derives a second solution, e.g. $1.24$, and no others in range; Concludes with $y=0.329$ or $y=1.24$ radians.
